I am 49 years old. I never went to school, not one day. I have been farming for 30 years, since I was a young bride brought to this village. My mother-in-law taught me how to plant, and I learned the rest by watching others and doing it with my own hands. I have 3 mu of land in Quzhou County. Two mu I plant with wheat in the fall, and then maize right after the wheat comes off in June. One mu I plant cotton in the spring, for cash money. My household has five people — my husband, me, my son and his wife, and our grandchild. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends some money back, but the farm is still our root. Every jin of fertilizer is real money out of my pocket.

I don't read books and I don't trust those people who come from the city talking fancy. I trust what I see with my own eyes. Last year my wheat got about 1000 jin per mu, the maize got about 1200 jin per mu, and the cotton was okay. This year I will do the same as last year, because change is risky and I cannot afford to guess wrong. Old Wang next door has 4 mu and his crops always look good, so I follow what he does and adjust down a little since my land is smaller.

For wheat: I plant improved wheat seed, the kind everyone buys from the seed dealer at the market. Before planting in October, I rotary till the field to make it soft. I put one full 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu as the base. Then in the spring, when the wheat turns green, I spread half a bag of urea on each mu. That is one bag of compound and half a bag of urea per mu total. I don't measure in kilograms, I measure in bags. I would rather put a little too much than too little — a bad harvest means my family goes hungry, but wasting some fertilizer is just money down the drain. I irrigate three times from the well: once when it greens up, once when it shoots up tall, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide twice. If the weather is fair like last year, I expect 1000 jin per mu, which is 500 kg.

For maize: After we harvest the wheat in early June, there is no time to waste because the season is short. I plant hybrid maize seed straight into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. I put 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time. Then when the corn is about knee-high, I topdress with 20 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate twice in the summer, because July and August can turn dry quick. Two pesticide sprays. I expect about 1200 jin per mu, which is 600 kg.

For cotton: I plant 1 mu of improved cotton seed in the spring. I rotary till first to break up the soil. I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. Then I topdress twice with urea, about 7 or 8 jin each time, roughly 15 jin total per mu. Cotton needs water when it flowers, so I irrigate twice. But the bugs love cotton more than the other crops, so I spray three times. I hope to get 600 jin of seed cotton per mu, which is 300 kg.

Everything costs more this year. Compound fertilizer is over 150 yuan a bag, and urea keeps going up too. But I have to put it in. If I skip fertilizer to save money, I might get nothing, and then what will we eat? So I do what I did last year. That is my plan.
